facts.text: Washington, Louisiana, founded in 1720 as a French trading post on Bayou Courtableau, is the state’s third‑oldest settlement.
Steamboats once raced up Bayou Teche to Washington, but a tight bend at the port made turning impossible, creating a historic bottleneck.
Every year, Washington celebrates the Washington Catfish Festival, a lively event that evolved from the town’s former Festival du Courtableau.
The Old Steamboat Warehouse on Bayou Courtableau, just upstream from the turnaround, reminds us of the steamboat era that ended with the railroad in the late 1800s.
Washington was officially incorporated in 1835, adopting its current name after evolving from the post of Opelousas.
About 80 percent of Washington’s historic homes and businesses are listed on the National Historic Registry, preserving a 19th‑century Louisiana atmosphere.
